text:
maria: Quick a11y follow-up from today's design review — the Settings > Model tuning form accordion is surprising for keyboard users. When you open the accordion and tab into inputs, closing (ESC or click) leaves focus in the body instead of returning to the accordion header. Users lose place.

maria: Repro: tab to header (keyboard), Enter to expand, Tab into first input, then press ESC or click close. Expected: focus goes back to the header (the trigger). Actual: focus lands on document/body and you have to tab a bunch to get back.

maria: Proposed fixes (short):
- Ensure the accordion header is the focus target on close (focus return).
- Toggle aria-expanded on the header button and add aria-controls to point at the panel.
- Panel should have role="region" + aria-labelledby referencing the header.
- If there's a close button inside the panel, keep it in logical DOM order but manage focus: opening should focus first interactive inside, and closing should focus header.

maria: Tiny code hints we discussed:
```js
headerButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const expanded = headerButton.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  headerButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!expanded));
  if (!expanded) { panel.querySelector('input, select, button')?.focus(); }
});
// on close (esc or close button) -> headerButton.focus();
```

tyler: +1 — also make sure Space works the same as Enter for the header button. And arrow keys between adjacent accordion headers (roving pattern) would be nice for dense lists. @eng FYI. :thumbsup:

avni: One more: validation errors inside the accordion need to be announced when they appear. If a save fails, move focus to the first invalid field OR add an aria-live polite container that includes a short summary (e.g., "2 errors in Model tuning"). Screen reader users can otherwise miss the context. Also dark theme needs a stronger focus ring on the header — contrast low at 2px.

design-bot: Automated check: "color-contrast" flagged the focus outline token -- fails AA when 2px on #0f172a background. Suggest increasing thickness or changing token to a11y-focus-strong.

sam: I'm going to add acceptance criteria to the ticket in JIRA:
1) Focus returns to header on close (keyboard + click).
2) aria-expanded toggles correctly and aria-controls present.
3) Panel has role=region and aria-labelledby.
4) Errors announced (aria-live OR focus move).
5) Arrow-key roving between headers optional (degs).
6) Axe run + visual focus check in dark/light.

jim: I'll pick this up on the frontend side. Quick question on behavior when accordion contains a modal-triggering control: if the user opens a modal from inside the panel, on modal close should focus go back to the trigger inside the panel (preferred) or to the accordion header? My vote: return to the element that opened the modal. We should document both flows. @maria @avni

maria: Agreed — modal should return to opener inside panel. Only when panel itself collapses should focus go to header. We should add both cases to the test matrix.

tyler: Can we add a tiny demo page in storybook showing keyboard flow + screen reader cues? That would make QA faster.

sam: Yep — I'll add stories: "Accordion: keyboard focus return", "Accordion: error announce", "Accordion: modal opener focus return". Also include a11y regression e2e for tab flow.

maria: Thanks all. I'll update the design notes and attach a short voiceover test script for QA. Pasting quick SR script: 
- Tab to header -> Enter open -> Tab into first field -> Enter invalid value -> Save -> listen for error announcement -> ESC to close -> confirm focus on header.

jim: Cool. ETA: PR by next Wed.

design-bot: Note: created ticket: DESIGN-1428 "Form accordion: keyboard focus memory & aria improvements" (assigned to @sam, priority P2).

maria: :heart: closing loop. LMK if anyone spots edge cases (nested focus traps, virtualization).
